newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude mixed as Minas weakens, MidEast steady.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude mixed as Minas weakens, MidEast steady.

text.p: Asian crude oil prices were mixed on Wednesday, as Minas weakened, Bach Ho firmed and Middle East grades were steady.
A correction in Brent Tuesday prompted the Brent/Dubai to narrow while expected demand from India for October Dubai crude helped support the Dubai intermonth spreads.
The Brent/Dubai was assessed in Singapore at $1.60/$1.65 per barrel for October, compared with $1.65/$1.73 on Tuesday.
Intermonth Dubai swaps rose two or three cents. Oct/Nov was assessed at 35/45 cents from a day-earlier 36/40 and Nov/Dec was assessed at 35/42 cents from 33/38 cents.
Brokers said a Japanese refiner bought three October Dubai swaps at $17.80, $17.83 and $17.85. But they said the purchases related to crack spreads, rather than direct crude hedging.
Paper Tapis levels were steady with September at $20.40/$20.65 versus a day-earlier $20.45/$20.75 while October maintained a 20-cents backwardation.
A Japanese trader was said to have sold 150,000 barrels of Minas to China at ICP minus 35, the lowest price to date for September barrels.
Most deals have been done between 25 and 30 cents below the ICP.
But 350,000 and 450,000 barrels of Bach Ho were said to have traded at OSP minus 20 cents, up 10 cents on the last deal done.
MidEast barrels were steady. A 250,000-barrel cargo of Lower Zakum was traded at ADNOC plus 15 on Monday and 500,000 barrels were traded at plus 16 cents on the same day.
A partial Murban traded at ADNOC plus 15 cents between a Japanese refiner and a U.S. major. It was their second October deal for a partial cargo, traders said.
